en:
So it's finally my turn?
Nice to meet you all.
My name is Shoji Arai, from Class 2-B.
...Still, you were all chosen from the whole school, and it shows. You know all sorts of scary stories.
I'm truly impressed.
I know a fair number of scary stories myself, but I'd started to feel a little uneasy.
What would I do if someone else told the story I'd prepared before I could...?
But it seems there was no need at all for that worry.
After all, this school has mountains of scary stories...
Well then, let me begin my story.
Have any of you heard of 'the Three O'Clock Hag'?
Ah... it seems a few of you have.
...{a}.{p}What about you?
I know it well
I only know the name
I've never heard of it

The Three O'Clock Hag is apparently a yokai that appears in restrooms at exactly three in the afternoon.
...That said, all you hear are stories of someone hearing a hoarse voice, or of a stain shaped like an old woman appearing on the wall. It seems no one has ever actually seen the yokai itself.{p}
Restroom stories aren't my specialty, so I don't know much about them myself.

So then, why did I bring up a story like that...?
The truth is, there's one at this school too.
A yokai that appears when three o'clock comes......
That yokai...
I call it 'the Three O'Clock Phantom,' but it seems very few people know it exists.
Well, that's only natural.
This Phantom very rarely shows itself, you see.
For the Three O'Clock Phantom to appear, a certain condition has to be met.
And that condition is...{p}{a}, what do you think it might be?
There's a special day for it
There's a special clock
There's a special ritual

Did you already know this story...?
That's right.{p}
They say the Three O'Clock Phantom appears only when 'a certain clock' in this school points to three.{p}

Ever since I heard the rumor of the Phantom, I've been searching for that clock.
I asked all sorts of people about it, went around checking every clock in the school...
The classrooms, of course, and the faculty room, the principal's office, everything from the art room to the nurse's office...
I even checked the clocks in the off-limits old school building, one by one.
Even so, I never found the clock where the Phantom is said to appear.
Was the rumor a lie after all...★
Just as I'd begun to think so, I was finally able to track down where that clock was.{p}

Everyone, please look at that wall.
There are two clocks hanging side by side, aren't there?
One of them is running properly.
Right now it's... oh, is it this late already?
At this rate, it'll be quite late by the time all the stories are finished.
I'll tell mine a little faster.
Yes, that one is an ordinary clock.
There's no need to pay it any special attention.
What matters is the other clock.{p}

It's covered in dust, and there's no sign of it moving at all.
Is it broken, perhaps...?
But I'll say it with certainty.
That clock is the very clock that can summon the Three O'Clock Phantom!{p}
{a}...{p}Sorry, but would you take that clock down for me?
Take down the running clock
Take down the stopped clock
Take down neither clock

...Thank you.
Everyone, please watch the clock's hands.{p}

They're pointing to 2:59.
In other words... one minute to three.
When these hands point to three...
the Three O'Clock Phantom should appear.{p}

Well then, shall we go ahead and summon the Phantom?
It's simple.
All it takes is moving the clock's hands a little.
Now, {a}.{p}Move the hands, please.
Move them
Don't move them
Don't move them
I want Arai to move them

That's it, turn that knob...
...Just a little.
Just a tiny bit...

Did you hear that?
Just now, there was definitely a click, wasn't there?

The hands gave a little twitch...
...Sorry, I seem to have gotten rather excited...{p}

Ah... it's three o'clock, all right.
The clock is pointing to three.{p}I wish the Phantom would hurry up and appear...
I'm sure it'll appear
I don't think it'll appear
I don't know

You're quite the lover of scary things yourself.
Then again, I suppose only that sort of person could cover the seven wonders...
Of course, I think it'll appear too.

You could even say I believe it.
This time, the Phantom will really appear...
...Somehow, it's thrilling.
I've never had this much fun before.{p}

Oops, I shouldn't be calling it fun.
According to one theory, the reason no one has ever seen the Phantom is that everyone who saw it was killed by it... or so they say.
At this school, teachers and students have been dying mysteriously or going missing, again and again, for a long time.
Apparently, a few of them were interested in the Three O'Clock Phantom, just like me...
That's probably where the rumor started spreading from.
...It's a frightening story.
Well, it's only a rumor, of course.{p}

Still...
...It's really taking its time to appear.
No one told me it would take this long.
Was the rumor of the Three O'Clock Phantom a lie?{p}Or did I pick the wrong clock?
I think the rumor was a lie
I think you picked the wrong clock
If we wait a little longer, I'm sure the Phantom will appear

...But let's give up for today.
It's not good to stay at school too late, after all.
Well then, this brings my story to......
Just as Arai said this and looked down...!{p}

"Eeek!"
Suddenly, a girl screamed.
"Someone was peeking in just now!"
The girl had gone pale and was pointing at the door.{p}

...Huh?
That was strange.
The door was half open.{p}It had been shut tight until just a moment ago...
Go close the door
Wait and see what happens

I reached for the knob to close the door.
At that moment...☆{p}

"Aaagh!"
I found myself screaming.{p}

Beyond the narrow gap in the door, there was definitely something.
Its face was in shadow and hard to make out, but its red, bloodshot eyes were glittering fiercely.{p}
The moment its eyes met mine, it spun around and started running.
Chase it
Don't chase it

I have to go after it!
That must be the Three O'Clock Phantom!
I rushed out into the hallway.
...And there was the man, like a black shadow, wavering like a heat haze as he turned the corner of the hallway.
In just an instant, he was already that far away...
"What's wrong, {a}?"
Without even turning back at the voice calling after me, I ran as hard as I could.{p}

I rounded the corner of the hallway a moment behind the Phantom.
...Stairs.
One flight led up to the floor above, and one led down to the floor below...{p}Which way had the Phantom vanished?
Go up the stairs
Go down the stairs

"Whoa!"
With a lurch, my foot missed the step, and my body was flung out into the air.
The scenery around me seemed to turn slowly, and the next instant, the floor of the landing was rushing up at my face.

There was a heavy thud, and searing pain shot through my arms, my back, my legs.
First a sharp pain.
Then a pain that seemed to seep out, slowly...
The consciousness I was barely clinging to would slip away the moment I let go.{p}

A shrill voice, as if mocking me, echoed from out of nowhere.
Feeling that laughter echo deep inside my ears, I sank deeper and deeper into unconsciousness...{p}

...It seemed I'd passed out.
How much time had gone by...?
"Are you all right?
Stand up slowly..."
Holding on to the hand Arai offered me, I staggered to my feet.
...Throb.
As my head cleared, the feeling came back to my arms and legs.
I could walk, but even the slightest movement sent sharp pain through my joints, and moving my body was a terrible chore.
"Um... {a}?"
Letting go of my arm, Arai asked hesitantly.{p}"...Were you able to see the Three O'Clock Phantom?"
Answer yes
Answer no

"...I see.
A black shadow... huh...
As an article on the seven wonders, I feel it lacks a little impact..."
Disappointment was plain on Arai's face.{p}

But he soon broke into a smile.
"Still, we have to be glad you made it out alive.
After all, many people have lost their lives after meeting the Phantom.
...Now, let's go back to the newspaper club.
Everyone's waiting for us.
If the seventh one doesn't come, the next story will be the last."{p}

Arai gave a lonely smile and slowly began to climb the stairs.
...That's right.
I had to hurry back to the club room.
That shrill laughter still lingered deep in my ears...
I climbed the stairs as if to shake that voice off.{p}

You know it well?
So the Three O'Clock Hag is a fairly famous yokai, then.
...It's embarrassing to say this after bringing up the name myself, but I don't know much about the Three O'Clock Hag.
Just the name and a few rumors, I suppose...{p}

That's about all I know.
...Restroom stories aren't my specialty.{p}

Oh, you've never heard of it...?
The Three O'Clock Hag is a fairly well-known yokai, you know.
I didn't think there was anyone these days who didn't know it...
Well, that's a surprise.
If you're any kind of newspaper club member, maybe you should make more of an effort to gather information.
...That said, I'm in no position to lecture anyone.
The truth is, I don't know much about the Three O'Clock Hag myself.
Just the name and a few rumors, I suppose...{p}

Yes, that's all I know.
...Restroom stories aren't my specialty.{p}

A special day, you say...
So you think the same way I do, {a}.
That the Phantom might appear at three o'clock only on days that carry some kind of meaning, like Friday the 13th...
I thought so too, at first.
But that guess is wrong, I'm afraid.
...Too bad.{p}

According to the rumor, the Three O'Clock Phantom needs a special clock in order to appear.
They say the Phantom appears only when 'a certain clock' in this school points to three.{p}

Yes...
Actually, that's right.
It's nothing so grand that you'd call it a ritual, but summoning the Phantom requires a certain special procedure.
...Yes, I know that procedure.
When people heard I was going around looking into 'the Three O'Clock Phantom,' they offered me all sorts of information...
...And among all that was a terrifying story, one you must never hear.
A terrifying story you must never hear.
{a}...{p}Do you have the courage to hear this story?
Yes, I do
No, I don't
I see. Then I'll tell it to you.{p}

Once, there was a P.E. teacher at this school named Adachi.
"Studying is important, but it isn't the only thing school is for."
...That was the coach's philosophy, and apparently the students adored Coach Adachi.
But then, one day...
all of a sudden, there was an incident.{p}

...The cause was failing his entrance exams.
It was the time of year when the third-years had retired from their clubs to study for exams, but...
that student loved running, and apparently he kept showing up at practice now and then.
For that, the student's parents blamed Coach Adachi viciously.
"It's your fault my son killed himself!
He failed to get into college because he kept doing track...
What happens to a student who gets distracted by anything but studying at this time of year...
surely even a teacher knows that?
Why didn't you scold him more strictly?☆"{p}

That mother's anguished cry must have pierced Coach Adachi's heart deeply...
Feeling heavily responsible, Coach Adachi spent night after night unable to sleep.
Day and night, the coach was racked with self-blame...
until finally, driven to the edge, the coach committed suicide.{p}

All sorts of stories have been passed around about how the coach did it.
According to one person I heard from, the coach died by hanging in the old school building.
According to another, the coach jumped from the roof.
Some say the coach ran out into the road and was hit by a car, while others say the coach died after drinking a deadly chemical.
With this many theories, I haven't the faintest idea which one is true.{p}

Strangely, though, no matter whose story you hear, they all say the coach died at three in the morning.
It was an unfortunate incident that happened back when people had started talking about the 'exam wars.'{p}

...{a}.
That's all there is to the story you must never hear.
You seem let down.
But this is no time to be feeling that way.
You see...
the people who told me this story have been falling victim to the Three O'Clock Phantom, one after another.
Some have died...
Some have shut themselves away in their own world...
Nearly all of them have met a miserable fate.
The Three O'Clock Phantom shows itself to whoever hears this 'story you must never hear' for the first time.
And of all of you, the one hearing this story for the first time is......
Oh...?
It seems you're the only one, {a}.
So everyone else already knew the proper steps of the ritual...{p}

Well then...
From here on, I'll speak for your ears only, {a}.
...Are you ready?
Remember well what I'm about to tell you.
Without fail, sometime tonight... at three o'clock tomorrow morning, to be exact, the Phantom should appear in this room.
You must linger here and wait for it.
All by yourself... mind you.
Lingering all alone in this empty club room, waiting for the Phantom...{p}...Understood?
Understood
No way, I don't want to

Oh my, you've got more nerve than you look.
Then the first stage of the ritual should succeed.{p}

...Listen.
They may be called Phantoms, but they were originally people, just like us.
Whether it's Coach Adachi or the track team student...
both of them are pitiful spirits who can't pass on because they killed themselves.
So they appear, relying on the people who have heard the story.
They long to be given a memorial, you see.
When the Phantom appears before you, it will surely state a single wish.
It might be water, or a flower they loved, or some kind of food...{p}

You must indulge that wish and grant it.
While praying that they may pass on as soon as possible...{p}...Understood?
Understood
No way, I don't want to

I see...
You're a kind person.{p}

'Indulging' their wish is the most important part of the ritual.
And then comes the finishing touch.
Yes, once you've come this far, the rest is easy.
You simply close your eyes gently and chant a certain spell.
It's not a very difficult spell.
Just a single word.
Kotodama, I suppose you might call it...
They say that short word itself holds a special power.
The word is 'Ea.'
It's an ancient sacred word, said to mean purification...
At the very end of the ritual, you chant the holy word.{p}...Got that?
Understood
No way, I don't want to
...I see.

Hearing you say that puts my mind at ease.
Now then, be sure to follow every step properly.
Linger...
Indulge...
Ea...
Those three.
...All right?
Well then, everyone...
It's a real shame, but since {a} now has to wait for the Three O'Clock Phantom, let's call it a day here.
I'd like to leave our friend in peace, to focus quietly alone...{p}So let's head home now, so we don't get in the way.
Ask them to stay
Just watch them go
Oh, what's the matter?{p}Could it be that you've gotten scared?
I got scared
No, not at all

I suppose not...
After all, {a}, you were chosen out of the many newspaper club members to be here and hear scary stories.{p}

You want to savor a lot more fear, don't you?
I understand that feeling very, ve-ery well.
Unless someone loves scary things that much, they could never wait for the Three O'Clock Phantom alone.
Very well, let's continue the seven wonders.
I'm not quite sure whether the seventh person will show up, but...
there's still plenty of time left until three in the morning, when the Phantom appears.
Now then, shall we hear the next person's story?{p}
You don't?{p}

...I see.
I can't believe you lack courage, though...
Perhaps somewhere inside, you sense the danger lurking in this story.
Well then, it's a shame, but that's the end of my story.
Here, after all, what {a} says goes...{p}

Without {a} knowing...
It's a method with quite a long tradition behind it.
Hm hm hm hm hm...
Yes, you can look forward to its effects, too.
...Just keep it a secret from {a}, mind you.
Hm hm, hm hm hm hm hm...
Now then, let's have you move on to the next story.
...Oh, isn't the next person the last one?
I wonder what happened to the seventh one...{p}

That won't do.
This is extremely important.
Otherwise, {a}...
you'll lose your life.
...Understood?
You absolutely must wait for the Phantom.
...Yes, that's how it should be.{p}

That won't do!
I can't allow that.
{a}...
Don't you value your own life?
...Understood?
You absolutely must indulge the Phantom's wish.{p}

That won't do.
Why can't you promise something this simple?
Without this spell, the ritual won't succeed.
You'll die, you know.
...Understood?
At the very end of the ritual, you must chant the spell 'Ea.'{p}
At Arai's words, everyone began getting ready to go home.{p}

"See ya."
"Bye-bye."
One after another they said their goodbyes and left the club room.
And last of all, Arai stood in front of the door.{p}

With a meaningful smile, he said this:
"...Well then, {a}.
Goodbye...
I'll pray that you live to see tomorrow morning safely."{p}

Once the door closed and I was alone, the room suddenly turned chilly.
Just a moment ago, I'd even thought it was muggy...
The clock on the wall still said it wasn't even ten yet.
There was still plenty of time until three in the morning, when the Phantom would appear.
Okay, while I've got the chance, I'll properly review the ritual steps Arai taught me.{p}If I remember right, the very first thing I have to do is......
Linger, waiting for the Phantom
Indulge the Phantom's wish
Chant the holy spell

...Right, right, the first step was to linger, waiting for the Phantom.
Which is exactly what I'm doing right now.
Um...{p}What came after that?
Indulge the Phantom's wish
Chant the holy spell

...Right, right, the second step was to indulge the Phantom's wish.
Okay, I'll grant any wish at all.
But...
I hope it doesn't wish for anything too hard...
And finally, I had to chant the holy spell.
Yeah, I'm fine.
I've got it all memorized.
...The Phantom can show up any time it likes.{p}
An hour passed......{p}

...Linger, waiting for the Phantom.
...Indulge the Phantom's wish.
And the holy spell, Ea...
So these three make up the all-important ritual that protects me from the Phantom...{p}
Two hours passed......{p}
...It's still not three.{p}
Three hours passed......{p}

...Linger for the Phantom.
...Indulge the wish.
...The spell called Ea.
These three are what matter.{p}
Four hours passed......{p}
Five hours passed......{p}

"Linger.
Indulge.
Ea...!"
In my excitement, I'd shouted it out loud.
And then...
"......★"{p}

Linger..., indulge..., Ea...?
L... I... E...
L-I-E...
...Wait, this is...!{p}

"A big, fat LIE!"
There was no Three O'Clock Phantom, not anywhere...
"Ugh..."
Arai had fooled me but good.{p}

"Waaaaah!☆"
My scream, from the very bottom of my heart, echoed through the school building in the night.{p}

And at that very moment there was a click, and every clock in the school was pointing to three.
It was the moment a new legend of the Three O'Clock Phantom was born.
"They say that at three in the morning, an eerie scream comes from the school building, where no one should be...
and that it's the voice of the Three O'Clock Phantom......"{p}

No, something feels wrong about that...
Let me think it over again.{p}

Hmm, I feel like I've got something mixed up.
Let me think it through carefully once more.{p}

My, my, you really are hopeless.
It's a true wonder that someone like you manages to cover the seven wonders.
I was thinking of leaving you here alone and going home, but I've just changed my mind.
Very well, we'll stay here with you.
And let's carry on with the seven wonders, shall we?
Luckily, there's one person left.
I'm not quite sure whether the seventh person will show up, but...
there's still plenty of time left until three in the morning, when the Phantom appears.
We'll have {a} experience something even more frightening.
That's what you want, isn't it?
...{a}.
Now then, shall we hear the next person's story?{p}

No, {a}.
Not that clock.
I meant the stopped clock next to it.{p}...Would you take it down for me?
Take it down
Don't take it down

You won't take it down for me?
And here I am, asking you so earnestly...
You're quite a mean person, aren't you, {a}?{p}Don't you want to see the Phantom's true identity for yourself?
I do
I don't

You do...?
You definitely just said so.
So you want to see the Phantom's true identity for yourself, too!
Then please take the clock down.
I won't let you say no.
...Understood?
Come on!{p}

I see.
So you think differently from me, {a}.
...What a shame.
Well then, it can't be helped.
Let's give up on summoning the Phantom.
Everyone, that is the end of my story.
My apologies to those of you who were looking forward to meeting the Three O'Clock Phantom, but at today's meeting, {a}'s word is absolute.
Oh...?
Everyone, you look rather dissatisfied.
In that case, I'll teach you a way to resolve that dissatisfaction later.{p}

Without {a} knowing...
It's a method with quite a long tradition, you know.
Hm hm hm hm hm...
Oh yes, you can look forward to the results, too.
...It's a secret from {a} alone, after all.
Hm hm, hm hm hm hm hm...
Now then, let's move on to the next story.
...Oh my, isn't the next person the last one?
I wonder what happened to the seventh one...{p}

What's the matter, {a}?
Don't tell me you've gotten scared now, at this point...
...You aren't going to say that, are you?
Saying that won't do you any good.
If you won't move them, I'll move them myself.
Lend me the clock, please...{p}

"...Huh★
You're saying you want me to move them?"
"Yes, that's right.
I really think something like this should be left to a senior.
Please, Arai, you move them."
It was a golden chance, sure, but Arai was far better suited to the role than I was.{p}

"R-really...?"
"Yes, absolutely."
"Well then, I won't hold back..."
With that, Arai bashfully reached for the clock, and just as he did...{p}

...Huh?
The hands moved before he had even touched them.{p}

What on earth just happened★
"{a}..."
Arai was staring at the clock, wide-eyed, too.
...Was this the Phantom's doing as well?
He had to be thinking that.
Because I was thinking the same...
...But then.{p}

"Geez, what's with you two?
Why the shocked faces?"
One of the girl members poked her head out from behind the clock.
"You moved them?"
"That's right.
I mean, if we left it to you two, this story would never get anywhere."{p}

...I suddenly felt completely drained.
Apparently this girl hadn't noticed the friendship, the affection, or whatever it was that had just passed between Arai and me.{p}

"But...
It is three o'clock now, at least, isn't it?
The hand gave a little twitch..."
Though he looked disappointed, Arai's voice sounded a little excited.
I looked at the clock again.{p}

It was three o'clock, all right.
...But would the Phantom really appear?{p}
What are you saying, now of all times!{p}

...Aha.
So you got scared after all.
You're actually a coward, aren't you, {a}?
No, I'm not blaming you.
Observing people like you is rather entertaining, you see.{p}

I see...
So that's what you think, {a}.
...I'm a little disappointed.
I thought that you at least, {a}, would believe it, even if it was a false rumor...
Oh, but that doesn't mean I blame you, {a}.
I know perfectly well that rumors are unreliable things.
Even so, I end up believing them.
No matter how dubious the rumor is...
...I suppose you'd call me gullible.
It was the same this time...{p}

That may be so.
It's a rumor that's been passed down for a very long time...
It's hard to imagine the clock from back then would still be around, isn't it?
{a}...
I'm truly disappointed.{p}

I watched carefully.
One minute... two minutes...
The door stayed open a crack...
There was no sign of anyone on the other side.
Was it just her imagination?
If not, then whoever had been peeking must have been startled by her scream and run off.
"{a}. Hurry up and close the door."
Since nothing had happened for a while, she seemed a little relieved, but...
She still didn't seem comfortable with the door left open.
"All right."
I nodded lightly and got up from my seat.{p}

I hurriedly shut the door.
Chase that thing? No way!
That was a terrifying monster.
Every cell in my body was telling me so.
Had the others seen it?
Part of me wanted to ask, but I'd hold off for now.
Anyway, one more story and everyone would be done.
At least until then, I wanted to pretend it had all been my imagination.
"Arai, unfortunately it doesn't seem to have been the Phantom.
We're short on time, so let's move on to the next story."{p}

"I see...
If you say so, {a}, then it can't be helped.
But please wait a little before we move on to the next story.
If the Three O'Clock Phantom does not appear...
there is something I must do."
With that, Arai began to speak, haltingly, bit by bit.{p}

Up...!
Trusting my gut, I ran up the stairs.
Unlike the other staircases, if I remembered right, this one had no exits between this floor and the roof.
If I was lucky, I might be able to corner the Phantom...
With a faint hope, I quickened my pace.
But however far I climbed, I saw nothing that looked like it.
Further up...!
I picked up my pace even more and climbed the stairs.{p}

At last I came out onto the roof.
...But the Phantom wasn't there either.
Had it melted into the darkness of the night...?
As I looked around, the wind brushed my cheek.
It was lukewarm and a little damp... a clammy, sticky wind.
Maybe it was my imagination, but I even thought I caught a faint smell of blood mixed in.{p}

...Drip.
The instant I thought that, a dark stain spread at my feet.
Could this be... blood★
When I fearfully touched it with my finger, it felt slimy, and a metallic smell drifted up.
The liquid on my fingertip looked reddish even in the darkness of the night.{p}

...Trickle.
I felt something run down my cheek, and every hair on my body stood on end.
...There was no doubt.
This was blood...
And it was my own blood.
When, and where, had I cut myself?
That clinging wind blew again.{p}

At the same moment, a cut like a thin line ran across my palm.
Beads of red blood welled up from the wound at once, and in no time they came trickling out.{p}

...Snick.
Another cut opened.{p}

Snick, snick...
With every gust of that sticky wind, more cuts appeared on my body.
Was this the Three O'Clock Phantom's doing★
Either way, it was dangerous to stay here any longer.
I had to hurry back to the newspaper club.{p}

I hurried down the stairs.
I hadn't been able to get a clear look at the Three O'Clock Phantom, but...
...that was enough.
If the seventh one didn't come, the next story would be the last...
Once I'd heard it out, I'd go straight home.
I couldn't stay in a place like this any longer.{p}

"No.
Unfortunately, I didn't see anything like that."{p}

"...I see."
Arai muttered just that, then fell completely silent.
...There's no point staying here like this.
I managed to get to my feet on my own, urged Arai along, and went back to the club room.{p}

The remaining members were all sitting there, looking bored.
Arai was still silent.
...What should I do?
If Arai's story was over, maybe I should move on to the next one...
Just as I thought that, Arai, who had been silent all this time, suddenly spoke.{p}

{a}...
I'm truly sorry.

I can't let my story end like this.
I will take responsibility and summon the Phantom myself, you'll see.
